purpose: one record per SHADOW boundary run, so the skill measures its own effect instead of presuming it: known-class recurrence per wave must trend to zero as classes gate, and a curve that has not bent after three post-admission waves is itself a finding about the architecture. Every record is a point on curve(); the R7 decision reads shadow_driver.decidable(), which drops records whose boundary ends in -fixture, because a replay of a committed fixture says something about the fixture and nothing about whether the classes are gating - and left in, it occupies the newest slot the decline test and the floor guard both read.
subject_kinds: the subject field names the station the run served, and its vocabulary is the target ids of domain/observation-topology.json - never a second list here. A record naming a station that file does not carry reds as OBSERVATION_TARGET_UNGROUNDED, and the declining curve is sliceable by station because of this one field.
denominator: artifacts_swept is the number of files the pass walked, summed over the four artifact kinds, filled by scripts/shadow_driver.py from its own walk and available on no flag - a denominator a caller could supply is a denominator that can be typed. curve() stays the raw series and curve_rates() divides by this, because a raw sum reads a bigger wave as a regression and wave size varies at every wave (ed3c/skill-concerns#167).
supplied_versus_measured: the no-flag rule is about MEASUREMENTS and not about every input: no flag may supply anything shadow_driver.py could have measured itself, because a supplied measurement is indistinguishable from a typed one. A JUDGMENT the producer cannot take - a human verdict on a finding, say - has no other way in, and what makes one evidence is not that nobody supplied it but that it is bound to the bytes it judged and stales when they move (ed3c/skill-concerns#152). The two rules do not compete and neither licenses the other.
undenominated: records taken before ed3c/skill-concerns#167 carry no artifacts_swept and never will. Adding one now would be a guess wearing a measurement, so curve_rates() returns UNDENOMINATED for those waves rather than a number, and a wave with even one undenominated record is UNDENOMINATED whole - dividing a wave's entire recurrence by part of its sweep reads as a rate and is an artefact.
append_only: records are appended by scripts/shadow_driver.py --append-record and never rewritten. What one file state can carry is checked: scripts/validate_red_team.py requires every run_id to be the producer's ISO-8601 instant, to not go backwards and to not repeat, so a typed label, a record inserted before an existing one, or the same pass counted twice all red. The producer refuses the second append itself as RECORD_ALREADY_APPENDED, which matters because a persisted report replays and equal instants are not backwards. The rest of append-only is carried by git history and branch protection, not by this sentence.
persisted_report: domain/persisted-reports/<wave>.json holds the producer's own report object, written by --save-report at the pass. --from-report derives the row from one of those through the same ledger_record(), so a record no longer has to be appended before the wave lands - which it did have to be, because landing mutates the bundle the producer would otherwise have to re-measure (ed3c/skill-concerns#158; #131's acceptance clause is what detects that). run_id is still the instant OF THE PASS, carried in the artifact. The artifact is committed at the boundary and git history is what says when it appeared; the hand-authored-report-artifact row of domain/residual-sensor-register.json is where the rest of that is registered.
unpersistable: a pass whose report was never persisted, and whose bundle has since landed, cannot produce a record at all. Those runs are listed with their reason in domain/unpersistable-runs.json rather than dropped, and they are never typed in: the numbers are exactly what was lost.
